paper.title_en: Global coherence: the genuine quantum resource in discord for quantum information tasks
paper.abstract_en: Quantum discord is an information-theoretic measure of non-classical correlations between quantum subsystems. It can assume nonzero values even for separable (i.e., non-entangled) mixed states and characterizes the specifically quantum component of correlations that is not captured by entanglement measures alone. Quantum discord does not capture genuinely quantum correlations in general. This work introduces the concept of global coherence to represent genuinely quantum correlations in discord. Global coherence in a bipartite system is defined as bipartite coherence that cannot be attributed to local coherence in either subsystem alone, and is operationally characterized by discordant states with a correlation matrix rank exceeding the minimum subsystem dimension. We introduce the resource theory of global coherence, in which any local operations of the form $\Phi _A \otimes \Phi _B$ are free operations, while classical randomness is not freely available. We establish that global coherence is necessary for semi-device-independent steerability, analogous to how entanglement is necessary for standard steering. Furthermore, for remote state preparation using two-qubit states, we identify a necessary and sufficient quantum resource by introducing a global coherence quantifier. Finally, we establish a hierarchy of correlations in bipartite quantum states and illuminate the relationship between coherence, discord, and entanglement. Our work clarifies the precise quantum resource underlying discord-based quantum information protocols and demonstrates that genuinely quantum correlation, as captured by global coherence, enables operational advantages beyond those achievable with locally coherent states.
